report:
**Conclusion:** 
Contrary to your initial expectation, scientific evidence indicates that regular intake of cranberry juice or cranberry extract **can** help prevent recurrent cystitis (urinary tract infections) in women prone to recurrent infections.

**Key Evidence:**

1. **Clinical Efficacy:** An updated 2023 Cochrane systematic review found moderate-certainty evidence that cranberry products (including juice, tablets, or capsules) reduce the risk of symptomatic, culture-verified UTIs in women with recurrent UTIs (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1550830724001526, https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2804706).

2. **Mechanism of Action:** Cranberries contain active compounds known as proanthocyanidins (PACs). PACs work by inhibiting p-fimbriated *Escherichia coli* (*E. coli*)—the predominant bacteria causing UTIs—from adhering to the urothelial cells lining the bladder (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37068952/).

3. **Clinical Guideline Support:** Professional medical organizations support cranberry intake as a non-antibiotic preventive strategy. The American Urological Association (AUA) guidelines state that clinicians may offer cranberry prophylaxis for recurrent UTIs in women (https://www.droracle.ai/articles/599751/is-cranberry-extract-effective-in-preventing-recurrent-urinary-tract).

In summary, regular consumption of cranberry products is an evidence-based non-antibiotic option that can effectively lower the incidence of recurrent cystitis in women.
